title: Managed Environments: the Power Platform governance tier, its licensing condition and its controls
summary: The sharing-limit automation note incorrectly says Microsoft's agent example covers only the security-group rule: the example also sets a viewer limit. The checked licensing conditions, deadlines and control commands are otherwise supported; the credential-sharing path omits the target selection, and the digest-recipient checklist step lacks a matching control row.

claims.claim: Managed Environments is a suite of premium Power Platform governance capabilities.
claims.quote: Managed environments are a suite of premium capabilities that allow admins to manage Power Platform at scale with more control, less effort, and more insights.

claims.claim: Managed Environments unlocks sharing limits, usage insights, maker guidance and environment-group rules.
claims.quote:
A managed environment encompasses, but isn't limited to, the following features:
- Environment groups
- Limit sharing
- Weekly usage insights
- Data policies
- Pipelines in Power Platform
- Maker welcome content

claims.quote: Admins can use managed environments with any type of environment.

claims.claim: Admins enable, disable and edit Managed Environments in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: The non-exhaustive Managed Environments feature list also includes solution checker and IP Firewall.

claims.claim: Sharing limits govern canvas apps, solution-aware cloud flows and agents.
claims.quote: If a user tries to share a canvas app, solution-aware cloud flow, or agent that contradicts the sharing rules, they're informed as shown.

claims.claim: Agent sharing limits control whether owners and editors can grant Editor permissions.
claims.quote: When selected: Owners and editors can share with any individual as an editor.When not selected: Owners and editors can't share with an individual as an editor.

claims.claim: Agent sharing limits control whether owners and editors can grant Viewer permissions.
claims.quote: When not selected: Owners and editors can't share with an individual as a viewer, nor can they share with a security group.

claims.claim: Agent sharing limits can prevent sharing with security groups.
claims.quote: If this setting is selected, owners and editors can only share with individuals as viewers. They can't share with a security group.

claims.claim: Agent sharing limits can cap the number of viewers.
claims.quote: If Only share with individuals (no security groups) is selected, you can control the maximum number of viewers with whom an agent can be shared with.

claims.where: What it is > Sharing limits; Why it matters

claims.quote: Sharing rules are enforced when users try to share an app, flow, or agent.

claims.where: What it is > Sharing limits; Risks and limits
claims.claim: Sharing rules do not remove access that existed before they were applied.
claims.quote: This restriction doesn't impact any existing users who already have access to the app, flow, or agent before the application of the sharing rules.

claims.claim: The weekly digest provides administrators with information about makers and resource usage.
claims.quote: Analytics about your top apps, your most impactful makers, and inactive resources you can safely clean up are distilled and delivered to your mailbox once a week.

claims.claim: Environment groups apply centrally configured rules across multiple environments.
claims.quote: Environment groups allow tenant administrators to define rules that automatically apply standardized settings or policies across all member environments.

claims.claim: Untouched group rules remain managed at environment level rather than becoming enforced group rules.
claims.quote: Untouched rules are managed at the environment level.

claims.claim: Agent sharing controls can be applied through environment-group rules.
claims.quote: You can configure these controls for an individual Managed Environment, or you can apply the sharing controls at scale using Environment Groups and Rules in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.quote: Power Apps Premium, Power Automate Premium, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Copilot Studio for Microsoft 365 Copilot (only for features related to Copilot Studio), Power Pages, Dynamics 365 Premium, Enterprise, Team Members, and Dynamics 365 Customer Insights.

claims.claim: Power Apps per app, Power Pages and Copilot Studio pay-as-you-go meters also qualify.

claims.claim: Activating Managed Environments makes qualifying standalone licences or meters a condition of active usage, not merely environment creation.
claims.quote: When you activate managed environments in an environment, all active usage requires one of these standalone licenses or pay-as-you-go meters.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; What to check
claims.claim: Every user running an app in a managed environment is in scope, including users of standard apps.
claims.quote: Every user who runs an app in a managed environment is in scope, including users who run standard apps. The requirement applies to active usage in the environment rather than to the type of app.

claims.claim: The Power Apps per app meter covers Power Apps usage only.
claims.quote: However, this meter covers Power Apps usage only; any Power Automate flow usage must be covered by standalone Power Automate licenses or Power Automate per flow plans.

claims.quote: Power Automate cloud flows that are triggered within apps or in context of apps or agents are covered by the respective Power Apps or Microsoft Copilot Studio standalone licenses.

claims.claim: The Developer Plan does not include the Managed Environments entitlement when users run their assets.
claims.quote: A managed environment isn't included as an entitlement in the Developer Plan when users run their assets.

claims.claim: Trial licences can license users in managed environments, subject to their own restrictions.
claims.quote: Trial licenses can license your users in managed environments, but the restrictions specific to these types of licenses still apply.

claims.claim: Microsoft gives 30 days as an example trial-licence restriction.
claims.quote: For example, trial licenses only license users for 30 days.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Risks and limits
claims.claim: From February 2027, users without an appropriate licence are blocked from opening apps in managed environments.
claims.quote: Starting February 2027, an appropriate license is strictly required for a user to open an app in a managed environment. If an appropriate license isn't assigned to the user, the app doesn't open

claims.claim: Apps are not removed from the environment when users are blocked for licensing.
claims.quote: Apps aren't removed from the environment, and access resumes after an appropriate license is detected.

claims.claim: Access resumes once an appropriate licence is detected.
claims.quote: Apps aren't removed from the environment, and access resumes after an appropriate license is detected.

claims.claim: An app, flow or agent out of compliance with sharing rules can only be unshared until it complies.
claims.quote: However, if an app, flow, or agent is out of compliance after rules are set, only unsharing is allowed until the app, flow, or agent is compliant with the new rules.

claims.claim: Sharing-rule enforcement can take up to an hour to start.
claims.quote: After sharing rules are set in the Power Platform admin center, it may take up to an hour for them to start getting enforced.

claims.claim: Sharing limits are enforced when sharing with individuals or groups in another team.
claims.quote: However, when a user attempts to share with individuals or groups in a Team other than the one bound to the environment, the sharing limits are enforced.

claims.claim: Removing an environment from a group preserves its last applied group configuration.
claims.quote: When an environment is removed, it retains the last applied configuration from the group's rules but becomes unlocked, allowing a local admin to modify it going forward.

claims.claim: Removing an environment from a group unlocks its settings for local administration.
claims.quote: However, its settings and policies are now unlocked, allowing the local environment admin to manage them directly.

claims.claim: Joining a group overrides local settings for published sharing limits, maker welcome content, solution checker, usage insights, backup retention and generative AI rules.
claims.quote: the corresponding settings at the environment level are overridden when added to the group: sharing limits, maker welcome content, solution checker, usage insights, backup retention, and generative AI settings.
